score_scale: 1–5, higher better; subjective screening judgments, not measured outcomes
synthesis: The strongest possibilities create commitments across organizations whose individual incentives cannot produce the useful outcome. Agents may lower the cost of specifying and maintaining those commitments. Neither agent superiority nor commercial demand was established here.

opportunities.name: Conditional transformer reserve rights for smaller utilities
opportunities.beneficiary_value: Small municipal and cooperative utilities obtain credible access to replacement large power transformers without each financing a complete independent reserve. Residents benefit from faster restoration. This concerns reserve access, not manufacturing inspection.
opportunities.missing_outcome: A utility can know before an emergency exactly which replacement it may call, under which simultaneous emergencies, with transport and owner-retention conditions already agreed.
opportunities.prior_art_and_specific_gap: GAO documents STEP, SpareConnect, RESTORE and Grid Assurance; pooling is established. SpareConnect leaves transaction terms bilateral, STEP has specified emergency triggers, and Grid Assurance owns inventory. GAO found limited smaller-utility participation. The narrower unproven gap is affordable, precommitted access to existing heterogeneous spares while preserving each owner's minimum protection. [S1]
opportunities.what_changed: GAO's May 2026 update still reports an open participation recommendation, while DOE is developing common-equipment information. Capable agents could maintain detailed evidence and agreement dependencies economically across small participants; that cost advantage remains a hypothesis. [S2]
opportunities.discovered_connection: Treat a spare as a bundle of mutually compatible contingent access rights. Combine technical compatibility evidence with cooperative risk allocation: a nameplate match alone cannot establish availability when several owners suffer together.
opportunities.minimal_construction_falsifier: Build a local rights ledger with explicit asset identifiers, technical evidence, dispatch deadlines, owner-retention rules and disaster scenarios. Enumerate allocations and emit either an auditable assignment or a concrete conflicting-claims witness. Then populate one class using public specifications; unknown compatibility must reject certification. Kill the opportunity if credible compatibility plus transport eliminates pooling savings, or an incumbent already offers equivalent terms economically to the target segment.
opportunities.commercial_mechanism: A utility association sponsors the pool; participating utilities pay annual reservation and administration fees, while contributing owners receive reservation revenue. Initial paid work would be engineering-backed feasibility. No willingness to pay, insurability or enforceability has been established.
opportunities.successor_inheritance: Versioned compatibility evidence, scenario exclusions, contract dependencies, counterexamples and verified commitments become reusable operational state. Successors can add participants without silently invalidating old promises.
opportunities.uncertainty: Moderate evidence of underserved users; low evidence of this precise product gap. Real inventories and binding commitments are unavailable. Older program descriptions require direct rechecking before launch.

opportunities.name: Conditional neighborhood commitments for shared thermal networks
opportunities.beneficiary_value: Residents, small building owners and municipalities obtain a financeable shared heating/cooling project where isolated retrofits and speculative studies leave collective infrastructure unbuilt.
opportunities.missing_outcome: A neighborhood can conditionally commit enough demand, access rights and anchor participation to justify engineering expenditure while capping each participant's tariff and cancellation exposure.
opportunities.prior_art_and_specific_gap: NYSERDA already supports stakeholder outreach, technical design, ownership and financing; DOE already funds community coalitions. The proposed gap is a single conditional closing arrangement linking those dependencies, rather than another feasibility report. Sources establish coordination work, not the absence of such contracts. [S3,S4]
opportunities.what_changed: DOE reports three installations progressing from eleven planning projects, supplying contemporary precedents. Agent-assisted comparison of building constraints, stakeholder terms and financing conditions may make smaller coalitions economical. No inference that the other eight projects failed is warranted. [S4]
opportunities.discovered_connection: Infrastructure financing resembles a threshold public-good problem: nobody should bear full early commitment risk before enough complementary participants join. An assurance contract can make a technically plausible cluster investable.
opportunities.minimal_construction_falsifier: Create a 12-building synthetic closing simulation with individual price ceilings, anchor withdrawal, easement failure and cost overruns. Require automatic cancellation/refund whenever any essential condition fails. Reconstruct one public pilot's disclosed economics. Reject if the arrangement cannot survive one plausible anchor exit, or if measured participation costs dominate savings. Real adoption requires later participant testing.
opportunities.commercial_mechanism: Municipalities or developers buy coalition formation; a project entity pays a closing fee only on financial close. Avoid relying on unspecified subsidies. Sales cycles, enforceable household terms and development liability may make the model unattractive.
opportunities.successor_inheritance: Carry forward stakeholder-condition graphs, bounded economics, withdrawal scenarios and locally reviewed terms; future agents update the coalition when a participant changes.
opportunities.uncertainty: Existing district-energy developers may already solve the proposed gap. Physical feasibility and financing remain dominant constraints.

opportunities.name: Joint purchase of prospective rare disease evidence
opportunities.beneficiary_value: Small patient foundations and competing therapy developers obtain otherwise underfunded, interoperable longitudinal evidence without duplicating scarce patients' reporting burden.
opportunities.missing_outcome: Several sponsors commit funding for one prospectively specified cohort and common measurements, governed by patients, with transparent access and cost allocation.
opportunities.prior_art_and_specific_gap: RDCA-DAP already standardizes shared data and governs access; recreating a repository has little novelty. Its FAQ distinguishes integration of existing data from collecting new prospective data and notes sustainability and consent obstacles. The proposed gap is joint financing of missing observations before they exist. [S5,S6]
opportunities.what_changed: FDA's March 2026 workshop explicitly examined fragmented rare disease data and legal/logistical sharing barriers. Agents could compare protocols and identify the smallest shared measurement set, but clinical validity still requires experts. [S7]
opportunities.discovered_connection: An advance purchase agreement can fund an evidence public good: multiple prospective beneficiaries finance common observations, while an existing trusted platform receives appropriately consented data.
opportunities.minimal_construction_falsifier: Using public protocols, choose one disease and map three sponsors' endpoint and eligibility requirements. Produce a prospective common dataset specification, consent requirements and cost allocation. Reject if incompatible populations or measurement schedules remove meaningful reuse. Synthetic bias tests cannot demonstrate that an external control is clinically valid.
opportunities.commercial_mechanism: Sponsors fund cohort operations and pay governance/service fees; patient organizations retain representation. No patient-data sale is required. Competitive incentives, consent, clinical costs and regulator acceptance can defeat the model.
opportunities.successor_inheritance: Preserve endpoint mappings, consent restrictions, protocol versions, missingness assumptions and documented reasons cohorts cannot be combined.
opportunities.uncertainty: Highest potential human value but weakest immediate validation. Existing consortia and registry providers may already supply the financing arrangement.

selected_opportunity: Conditional transformer reserve rights for smaller utilities
recommendation: Provisionally fund a two-day construction of the reserve-rights certificate and its adversarial scenarios. Continue only if one defensible equipment class offers economic headroom after transport, review and retained-owner protection. A successful synthetic ledger is necessary protocol evidence, not evidence of demand or executable physical reserves.

microconstruction_executed.method: Python exhaustively enumerated assignments for four synthetic utilities and all ten single/double-failure scenarios.
microconstruction_executed.fixture: Spare sA serves A/B; sC serves C/D; a hypothetical additional sX serves all four. Each spare serves one utility at a time.
microconstruction_executed.result: sA+sC cover 8/10 scenarios; simultaneous A/B and C/D are counterexamples. Adding sX covers 10/10.
microconstruction_executed.interpretation: Individual eligibility does not imply simultaneous reserve coverage. The universal spare is invented; these figures establish no real inventory reduction, engineering feasibility or market value.

limitations: All times UTC on 2026-10-27; first-batch query times are bounded, not individually clocked. Only primary sources support claims; secondary search hits were excluded. Six queries cannot establish novelty or exhaustive competition. No contacts, private data, external writes, customer commitments, physical validation or paid model campaign occurred. Two opportunities involve energy but differ in emergency reserve rights versus new neighborhood infrastructure; the third concerns prospective medical evidence.
